reason: The artifact is shareable and concrete: a high-value YouTube tutorial becomes a public-safe summary, workflow spec, and installable skill. The service must avoid transcript scraping and copied prompt packs.
first_traffic_source_plan: Existing GitHub and ClawHub skill audience
Demo posts showing one video converted into a skill without copying transcript text
Cross-link from Affiliate Video Campaign Operator and Agentic Video Production Publisher
trust_reason: Uses official YouTube metadata APIs for discovery
Transcript use is manual, creator-owned, or licensed
Every skill includes source receipt and public-safety review

share_trigger.user_feels: relief that a long video became an installable workflow
share_trigger.user_has: a summary, workflow YAML, source receipt, and skill folder
share_trigger.user_shares_with: AI operators, creator friends, or open-source maintainers
share_trigger.user_says: This turns useful YouTube tutorials into reusable skills instead of another notes file.
share_trigger.user_gains: status for packaging useful workflows and less repeated manual note-taking

free_mvp.giveaway: one manual video-to-skill conversion template and source-safety checker
free_mvp.first_10_users: Codex/OpenClaw users who already watch AI workflow tutorials
free_mvp.onboarding_prompt: Paste a YouTube URL, transcript or notes you are allowed to use, target agent, and desired skill name.

day_7.target: 1 complete demo conversion and 3 user reactions
day_7.shutdown_threshold: demo artifact is not useful enough to install

day_30.target: 3 published skills, 5 stars/installs, or 2 setup requests
day_30.shutdown_threshold: fewer than 5 qualified touches and no repeat use

day_60.target: 10 installs, 5 converted videos, or 1 paid setup

top_risks: YouTube transcript rights and scraping temptation
Generated skills become shallow summaries instead of executable workflows
Too broad a watchlist creates noise and manual review burden
smallest_next_experiment: Convert one operator-supplied transcript into summary.md, workflow.yaml, SKILL.md, and public-safety review before building a tracker.
